newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy not asking for delay to EMU - Prodi.
newsitem.headline: Italy not asking for delay to EMU - Prodi.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on Tuesday that Italy was eager to join European economic and monetary union (EMU) and was not seeking any delay to the launch of the single currency.

"Italy is not asking for EMU delay or changes," Prodi told a news conference. Earlier, Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini said a one-year postponement to EMU would have been helpful but impossible to negotiate at this late stage.
"Italy is ready and wants to enter from the start," Prodi said.
Italy has made huge efforts in recent years to tame tearaway government spending and halt the surge in state debt in a bid to bring its economy in line with Maastricht demands.
Prodi is due to unveil a further round of belt tightening this week with a package of measures aimed to cut up to 16 trillion lire ($9.5 billion) off the deficit.
The government says this will ensure that Italy's deficit will fall to the required three percent of gross domestic product (GDP) against 6.7 percent in 1996.
